1.scope: On 2026-10-28, by the maintainer’s decisions of that date, the first part of a machine-prepared, machine-audited and cross-family-checked candidate pack on how frontier-AI frameworks meet law was admitted: further provisions of the EU AI Act on general-purpose AI models, the initial draft of the EU Code of Practice (14 November 2024) with two comparisons with the final Code, the Commission’s Opinion on the Code, further provisions of China’s Interim Measures on generative AI, the Measures for Labelling AI-Generated Synthetic Content, two national standards, the 2025 amendment of the Cybersecurity Law and two filing announcements, and nine links from framework editions to the laws and commitments they name in their own words. A legal text states duties, not compliance; a filing or a listing is not an assessment of safety. All records remain seeds.

2.scope: On 2026-10-28, by the maintainer’s decisions of that date, the second part of the frameworks-to-law candidate pack was admitted with schema 2.19. Schema 2.19 adds countries keyed by their ISO 3166 code, the predicates introduced, passed, vetoed and revoked, document-level participant lists that say whether their count is stated by the source or counted by Selekoa, an announced stage for a revocation, a provision date computed from a rule the text states, and dated names on one entity for a renaming. The records concern summit texts from Bletchley Park to New Delhi with their participant lists as dated snapshots, the G7 Hiroshima code and the OECD reporting framework, UK memoranda with AI developers and the AI Security Institute’s renaming, US executive orders and their revocation, Commerce rules and NIST drafts, the AI Action Plan, and California, New York, Illinois and Michigan bills and statutes, together with the EU AI Act’s computed entry into force. Listing is not signature or compliance, absence from a list is not refusal, and a stated duty is not implementation. All records remain seeds.

fl-eu-cop-draft1-risk-types.statement: Measure 6.1 of the initial draft commits signatories to treat six types as systemic risks: cyber offence; chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear risks; loss of control; automated use of models for AI research and development; persuasion and manipulation; and large-scale discrimination.

time.note: Dated by the Commission’s publication of the initial draft on 14 November 2024.

fl-eu-cop-draft1-ssf.statement: Measure 7 of the initial draft commits signatories to adopting, implementing and making available a Safety and Security Framework detailing the risk management policies they adhere to in order to assess and mitigate systemic risks from their general-purpose AI models with systemic risks.
fl-eu-cop-draft1-ssf.qualification: A draft commitment; no one signed the draft. The draft continues by relating the Framework's comprehensiveness to the expected severity of systemic risks.

time.note: Dated by the Commission’s publication of the initial draft on 14 November 2024.

fl-eu-cop-draft1-ssr-before-market.statement: Sub-Measure 20.3 of the initial draft commits signatories to send the AI Office their Safety and Security Reports ahead of the decisions they pertain to, in particular before placing a new general-purpose AI model with systemic risk on the market.

time.note: Dated by the Commission’s publication of the initial draft on 14 November 2024.

fl-eu-cop-final-changes-from-draft1-risk.statement: The final Code's Appendix 1.4 specifies four systemic risks (CBRN, loss of control, cyber offence, harmful manipulation), where the initial draft's Measure 6.1 listed six types, including automated use of models for AI research and development and large-scale discrimination, which are not among the final four.

The record says only that the two types are not among the four specified risks. The intermediate drafts were not retrieved.

fl-eu-cop-final-changes-from-draft1-ssf.statement: The final Code's Safety and Security chapter opens Commitment 1 by committing signatories to a three-step Framework adoption process (creating, implementing and updating a “state-of-the-art” Framework) and to notifying the AI Office of it, where the initial draft's Measure 7 opened by committing signatories to adopting, implementing and making available a Safety and Security Framework.
